speaker_listener_roles_and_relationship.worker_resident: Warm, respectful adult-to-adult speech; use I/you and the person's stated name or form of address.
speaker_listener_roles_and_relationship.professionals_family: Known name or role; no invented age, gender or family relationship.

address_forms_and_conditions: Use natural requests such as Could I... and Would you like... when supported by the Japanese. Retain Haruko-san where that exact address is the learning target.
names_honorifics_and_unknown_gender_age: Names and neutral they/the person; no automatic Mr/Ms, Grandma/Grandpa, uncle/aunt, dear or childish terms.
register_and_social_phrases: Clear international English, consistent US spelling, complete connected sentences. The first-meeting yoroshiku greeting may be It's nice to meet you; do not add treatment promises.

preferred_terminology_by_concept_id.利用者: person receiving care; resident where the residential setting is explicit

person_reported_words.avoid: personal words (ambiguous about whose speech is being recorded)
person_reported_words.scope: Identify the care recipient explicitly when Japanese states 本人; do not apply to 自分の言葉 used for a learner explaining something in their own words.

headings_punctuation_and_script_fonts: Sentence-case headings and clear role labels; Japanese terms only for vocabulary or exact-address learning. Approved typography and script-appropriate fallback.
